title: Pantheos: an image-based WebGPU card game built with a long-running agent, plus its agent-produced trailer
author: _javas_crypt
selftext:
Disclosure: Pantheos is my own game and a personal experiment in delegating a complete game project to an AI agent. I provided the goals, design feedback and approvals; GPT 6.1 Sol did much of the implementation over roughly two weeks, running almost continuously on my machine. GPT Image Gen supplied the art and WebGPU handles the rendering.



The visual approach is mostly image-based. The worlds are images, as are the illustrations inside the cards. The cards themselves are 3D objects. Depth masks provide the apparent depth in the illustrations, and material masks control how light affects their surfaces. A practical constraint was to reuse the existing images and masks when improving the visuals. That kept the work focused on lighting, highlights, particles and interaction instead of replacing the art.



I reviewed movement and real play, including hand-card clarity and hover behaviour. The online editor exposes the card materials, depth effect, animation, particles, sound and voice setup. The trailer uses the same renderer as the game, shows a match with the actual in-game voices, manual booster opening, world transitions and that editor.



The trailer was another delegated task: GPT captured the game, edited the footage, produced the narration and performed the YouTube upload after my approval. I selected the narrator and requested a longer, slower cut. Existing music and sound credits are in the video description.



3:58 gameplay/tech demo: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZinWKtnVsqM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZinWKtnVsqM)



I'd value feedback on the image-based rendering: do the depth and lighting hold up when the cards move, and can you still follow the board during effects?
